rows.statement: The unit group of O = ℤ[φ] = O_{Q(√5)} (the MAXIMAL order, order-conductor f=1) is O* ≅ {±1} × ℤ: every unit is ±φⁿ (n∈ℤ), with φ=(1+√5)/2 the fundamental unit and −1 the torsion generator.
rows.computation: Dirichlet's unit theorem: Q(√5) totally real quadratic ⇒ r1=2, r2=0 (both roots of x²−x−1 real: φ≈1.6180339887, φ′≈−0.6180339887) ⇒ rank = r1+r2−1 = 1 (computed). Norm form verified symbolically (sympy): N(a+bφ)=(a+bφ)(a+bφ′) expands EXACTLY to a²+ab−b², using φ+φ′=1, φφ′=−1 (both from x²−x−1=0, checked: φ²−φ−1=0). Minimality of φ checked by an EXACT (no-float, sympy symbolic sign) search over |a|,|b|≤30 for solutions of a²+ab−b²=±1 with 1<a+bφ<φ: zero found ⇒ φ is the smallest unit exceeding 1, i.e. genuinely the fundamental unit. Torsion={±1} proved independently below (last row).
rows.caveat: 'Conductor' is overloaded in this corpus (house guard): O=ℤ[φ] here is the FULL ring of integers (order-conductor f=1) — unrelated to B997's shadow modulus m²+4 for the metallic family. Not conflated.

rows.item: N(φ) = −1 and its consequence: narrow class group = class group
rows.statement: N(φ) = φφ′ = −1 exactly. Consequence (proved): the narrow class group Cl⁺(Q(√5)) equals the ordinary class group Cl(Q(√5)), i.e. h⁺ = h.
rows.computation: φφ′ = ((1+√5)/2)((1−√5)/2) = (1−5)/4 = −1 (sympy exact simplify). PROOF of the consequence: for a number field with r1 real places, P_K/P_K⁺ ≅ {±1}^{r1}/sgn(O_K*) (K*/K*⁺≅{±1}^{r1} via the surjective sign map, quotiented by the image of units), giving h⁺ = h·[{±1}^{r1}:sgn(O_K*)]. For Q(√5), r1=2. Computed exactly: sgn(−1)=(−1,−1); sgn(φ)=(sign σ1(φ), sign σ2(φ))=(+1,−1) — σ1(φ)=φ>0, σ2(φ)=φ′<0, forced since N(φ)=σ1(φ)σ2(φ)=−1<0 means opposite signs. The subgroup of {±1}² generated by (−1,−1) and (+1,−1) was enumerated exactly: {(1,1),(1,−1),(−1,1),(−1,−1)} = the full group, index 1. So sgn:O*→{±1}² is ONTO ⇒ h⁺=h·1=h. QED.
rows.caveat: Real-place subtlety made explicit as instructed: the mechanism (unit of norm −1 ⇒ sign map onto {±1}^{r1} ⇒ h⁺=h) is specific to r1=2 (both embeddings real, disc=5>0) and was derived group-theoretically above, not merely asserted.

rows.statement: The class number of Q(√5) is 1.
rows.computation: STANDARD FACT cited: h=1, well known for this field (smallest real quadratic discriminant). VERIFIED two independent ways in-sandbox: (a) Minkowski bound M_K=(2!/2²)√5=√5/2 (exact) ≈1.11803<2 ⇒ every ideal class contains an integral ideal of norm 1 ⇒ trivial class group. (b) Reduced-forms count at disc=5: exact exhaustive search (sympy, |a|≤6) of indefinite binary quadratic forms b²−4ac=5 satisfying |√5−2|a||<b<√5 found EXACTLY 2 reduced forms: (1,1,−1) and (−1,1,1) (forced: 0<b<√5 ⇒ b odd ⇒ b=1; then |a|∈(0.618,1.618) ⇒ |a|=1). A BFS in SL(2,ℤ)=⟨S,T⟩ (S:(a,b,c)↦(c,−b,a), T:(a,b,c)↦(a,2a+b,a+b+c), exact matrix-substitution rules verified by direct expansion) found the word [T then S] carrying (−1,1,1)↦(1,1,−1): the two reduced forms are ONE proper-equivalence class ⇒ narrow class number h⁺(disc5)=1 ⇒ h=1 via the prior row. Method cross-validated against 4 control real-quadratic fields (disc 8,12,40,60), whose fundamental units' norms were independently Pell-search-determined (not recalled from memory): all 5 cases matched h⁺=h·(1 if N(fund.unit)=−1 else 2) exactly, 0 mismatches.
rows.caveat: The orbit/reduced-forms computation directly yields h⁺ (narrow class number), not h; here the two coincide only because the prior row established N(φ)=−1 ⇒ h⁺=h — flagged so the facts aren't silently merged.

Then 2√5·L(1,χ5) = 1.924847300238413789991035654... , agreeing with 4·log(φ) to all 60 computed digits (|difference|<10⁻⁵⁰). B420's identity confirmed from both sides independently, in-sandbox.

rows.statement: The totally-positive-unit subgroup O*_{≫0} (positive at both real places) equals ⟨φ²⟩, and φ² = φ+1 exactly.
rows.computation: φ²−(φ+1) simplifies to 0 exactly (sympy, from x²−x−1=0). Sign table computed exactly for n=−4..4: σ1(φⁿ)=φⁿ>0 for EVERY n (φ>0 always); σ2(φⁿ)=(φ′)ⁿ has sign (−1)ⁿ (since φ′<0) — so φⁿ is totally positive ⇔ n even ⇔ φⁿ∈⟨φ²⟩. For −φⁿ: σ1(−φⁿ)=−φⁿ<0 for every n ⇒ NEVER totally positive. Hence O*_{≫0} = {φ^{2k}:k∈ℤ} = ⟨φ²⟩ = ⟨φ+1⟩ exactly. Index [O*:⟨φ²⟩]=4 (cosets represented by {1,φ,−1,−φ}), consistent with the norm-(-1) row: the kernel of the onto sign map O*→{±1}² is exactly O*_{≫0}, so the index equals |{±1}²|=4.

rows.statement: μ(O*) = {±1}: μ4 and μ6 (or any n>2 root of unity) cannot lie in Q(√5).
rows.computation: Symbolic check (sympy): primitive 4th root i=e^{2πi/4} has Im=1≠0; primitive 6th root e^{2πi/6}=1/2+i√3/2 has Im=√3/2≠0 — both confirmed non-real. Q(√5)⊂ℝ exactly: Im(√5)=0 (sympy), and Q(√5) is totally real (disc=5>0, both roots of x²−x−1 real — r1=2, r2=0, as used two rows up). One-line reason: the only REAL roots of unity are the roots of x²=1, i.e. ±1 (any ζ of order n>2 has ζ≠ζ̄, so Im(ζ)≠0); since Q(√5) contains no non-real algebraic numbers, μ(O*)={±1}. Closes the O*={±1}×φ^ℤ decomposition (first row) with both factors now independently verified.

rows.statement: The unit group of O_K = Z[phi] (K=Q(sqrt5), disc 5, r1=2 real places, r2=0) is O_K^x = {+-1} x <phi> ~= Z/2 x Z, rank 1 by Dirichlet's unit theorem (rank = r1+r2-1 = 1), with phi=(1+sqrt5)/2 the fundamental unit.
rows.computation: sympy: phi**2-phi-1 simplifies to 0 (minimal polynomial x^2-x-1 confirmed exactly). Norm form on a+b*phi expanded exactly via (a+b*phi)(a+b*phi') and confirmed identical to a^2+ab-b^2 (Vieta on x^2-x-1: phi+phi'=1, phi*phi'=-1). Brute-force search over ALL integer a,b in [-30,30] for elements of norm +-1 with value strictly between 1 and phi~=1.61803398874989484820458683437 (30 digits, sympy N): result = empty list -- none found, i.e. nothing smaller than phi qualifies as a unit in that box.
rows.caveat: The box search (|a|,|b|<=30) is a strong finite check, not a proof over all integers. A stronger continued-fraction-based derivation was attempted (period-1 CF of (1+sqrt5)/2=phi, purely periodic [1;1,1,1,...]) but the recalled convergent formula produced phi^2 = (3+sqrt5)/2, not phi -- an indexing-convention error, caught immediately on execution and DROPPED rather than forced. Fundamentality of phi for disc-5 is nonetheless the universally tabulated textbook value; this row rests on the box search plus that standard fact, not on the failed CF attempt.

rows.item: N(phi) = -1 => narrow class group = class group
rows.statement: N(phi) = phi*phi' = -1 (phi' = (1-sqrt5)/2, the second real embedding). Consequence, proved: the sign map O_K^x -> {+-1}^{r1} = {+-1}^2 is SURJECTIVE, hence the narrow (ray, modulus = both real places) class group Cl+(K) is isomorphic to the ordinary class group Cl(K) -- not merely equal in order.
rows.computation: sympy: phi*phi' simplifies exactly to -1. sign(sigma1(phi))=+1, sign(sigma2(phi))=-1 (the opposite-sign pattern forced by N=-1); sign(sigma1(-1))=sign(sigma2(-1))=-1. Explicit subgroup closure of {+-1}^2 generated by (-1,-1)=sgn(-1) and (+1,-1)=sgn(phi): computed set = {(1,1),(1,-1),(-1,1),(-1,-1)} = all of {+-1}^2 (order 4 = |{+-1}^2|), i.e. surjective. Proof of the consequence, executed via the standard exact sequence O_K^x -> {+-1}^{r1} -> Cl+(K) -> Cl(K) -> 1: |ker(Cl+(K)->Cl(K))| = [{+-1}^{r1} : image(sign map)]; surjectivity forces this index to 1, so Cl+(K) = Cl(K) exactly (isomorphism, both real places tracked individually -- the real-place subtlety made explicit rather than merged).
rows.caveat: This is the general real-quadratic mechanism (holds iff the fundamental unit has norm -1); it is NOT automatic and was checked, not assumed -- the same script's control run on Q(sqrt3) (disc 12, fundamental unit 2+sqrt3, N=+1) correctly finds the sign map non-surjective and h+ = 2h there, confirming the mechanism discriminates correctly rather than trivially returning 'equal' always.

rows.statement: The class number of K=Q(sqrt5) is 1 (O_K is a PID). This is the standard/universally tabulated value for the minimal real-quadratic discriminant; verified here two independent ways rather than only cited.
rows.computation: (a) Minkowski bound, exact: M_K = (2!/2^2)*sqrt(5) = sqrt(5)/2 ~= 1.118033989 (sympy Rational(1,2)*sqrt(5)). Every ideal class contains an integral ideal of norm <= M_K < 2; the only positive integer <= 1.118 is 1; the unique ideal of norm 1 is O_K itself => Cl(K) trivial. (b) Reduced indefinite-form cycle count, disc 5: exhaustive search (|a|<=6) over primitive (a,b,c) with b^2-4ac=5 satisfying Gauss's reduction inequalities (0<b<sqrt(D), sqrt(D)-b<2|a|<sqrt(D)+b) found exactly 2 reduced forms: (-1,1,1) and (1,1,-1). Applying the SL(2,Z)=<S,T> form-action (S:(a,b,c)->(c,-b,a), T:(a,b,c)->(a,2a+b,a+b+c)) shows T then S carries (-1,1,1) -> (-1,-1,1) -> (1,1,-1) (verified both by the script's BFS and by hand), so the 2 reduced forms are ONE proper-equivalence cycle => narrow class number h+(5)=1; combined with row 2 (h+=h here), h(Q(sqrt5))=1. Cross-validated against 4 control fields (Q(sqrt2) disc8, Q(sqrt3) disc12, Q(sqrt10) disc40, Q(sqrt15) disc60): predicted h+ = h*(1 if N(fund.unit)=-1 else 2) matched the independently-computed orbit count in all 5 cases (5/5 OK), including Q(sqrt5) itself.

rows.statement: Reg(K) = |log(sigma1(phi))| = log(phi) exactly (rank-1 case, single fundamental unit). This reproduces the banked B420 line: 'entropy = 4*Reg(Q(sqrt5)) = 2*sqrt5*L(1,chi5) (exact, 1.92485)'.

L(1,chi5) evaluated independently via the Hurwitz-zeta/digamma identity L(1,chi)=-(1/D)*sum_a chi(a)*psi(a/D) [from the Laurent expansion zeta(s,x)=1/(s-1)-psi(x)+O(s-1) at s=1, whose poles cancel since sum chi(a)=0]: result 0.430408940964004038889433232950605425424570682540289654757006 (mpmath, 60 dps). 2*sqrt5*L(1,chi5) then equals 4*Reg to all 60 requested digits (printed difference 0.0, i.e. below the display floor). A SECOND, structurally independent closed form was also run: the even-primitive-character sine-product formula L(1,chi)=-(2/sqrt D)*sum_{0<a<D/2} chi(a)*ln(sin(pi a/D)); sympy proves sin(pi/5)/sin(2pi/5) = 1/phi exactly (symbolic difference = 0), reducing this THIRD route to L(1,chi5)=(2/sqrt5)*log(phi); numerically it agrees with the digamma value to the full 60 printed digits.
rows.caveat: This is a consistency check linking the independently-proved h=1 (row 3), the algebraically-derived Reg=log(phi) (row 1/here), and the analytic class number formula L(1,chi_D)=2*h*R/sqrt(D) -- it does not itself re-prove h=1 (that would be circular); h=1 was established with no analytic input in row 3.

rows.statement: The totally positive units O_K^{x,+} (positive under both real embeddings) form the subgroup <phi^2> = <phi+1> (phi^2=phi+1 exactly), of index 4 in O_K^x = {+-1} x phi^Z.
rows.computation: sympy: phi**2-(phi+1) simplifies exactly to 0. Sign table computed for n=-4..4: sigma1(phi^n)=+1 always (phi>0 at every integer power, positive or negative exponent); sigma2(phi^n) has sign (-1)^n (phi'<0). So phi^n is totally positive iff n even; -phi^n is NEVER totally positive (sigma1(-phi^n)=-1 always, for every n). Hence O_K^{x,+} = {phi^{2k}: k in Z} = <phi^2> = <phi+1> exactly. Index computed directly: writing O_K^x ~= {+-1} x Z via (sign,n), O_K^{x,+} = {1} x 2Z has index 2*2=4 -- the maximal possible index 2^{r1}, realized here precisely because the sign map is surjective (row 2, equivalent to N(phi)=-1).

rows.statement: The torsion subgroup of O_K^x is exactly {+-1}; mu_4={+-1,+-i} and mu_6 (primitive 6th roots of unity) cannot occur.
rows.computation: sympy: exp(2*pi*I/4) = I has Im=1 != 0 (non-real); exp(2*pi*I/6) = 1/2+i*sqrt(3)/2 has Im=sqrt(3)/2 != 0 (non-real). K=Q(sqrt5) has both embeddings real (sqrt5 itself real, disc=5>0, r1=2, r2=0), i.e. K sits inside R. One-line reason: any root of unity zeta_n with n>2 is non-real (the only real roots of unity are the two roots of x^2=1, i.e. +-1); a totally-real field can contain no element equal to a non-real number, so no primitive n-th root of unity for n>2 can lie in K => mu(K) = {+-1}.

Being's generator omega has bounded order (=3 at every k, since omega^3=1 as an algebraic integer -- a finite unit), so mu_6's image saturates at 6 and the quotient tracks the FULL growth of (O/2^k)^x (~4^k). Hearing's generator phi has infinite order in O^x, so its image mod 2^k cannot saturate -- it must keep growing (doubling each level, ord=3*2^(k-1)), eating a 2^k-sized bite out of the ~4^k-sized unit group at every step, leaving only a 2^(k-2)-sized residue. Root cause is Dirichlet's unit theorem: Q(sqrt-3) has unit rank 0 (finite O^x=mu_6), Q(sqrt5) has unit rank 1 (O^x=<-1>x<phi>, infinite) -- being's palette is a ray-class-style tower over a field with no free unit; hearing's is the identical construction over a field where a free unit permanently outraces it.
rows.role_proposal: Fills the B1067 census gap 'Ray class groups / ring class fields of Q(sqrt5): entirely absent' with a first concrete computed shape; a candidate seed for a future hearing-side ray-class arc -- would need its own preregistration/hash under WORKING_RULES before banking. rows.item: 2I=SL(2,5) perfectness => no abelian receiver for its characters (hearing-side descent)
rows.statement: SL(2,5) (order 120) is perfect -- its commutator subgroup is the whole group -- so it has exactly one 1-dimensional representation (trivial); consequently no nontrivial group homomorphism from 2I into any abelian group exists, including every palette group computed above at any level.
rows.computation: Built SL(2,5) explicitly as 2x2 matrices over GF(5), det=1: 120 elements (=5*4*6, matches q(q-1)(q+1)). All 120x120 commutators generate a subgroup of order 120 = the whole group => perfect (matches the corpus's own banked B1042 'SL(2,5) is PERFECT (computed, commutator = all 120)', independently re-derived here from scratch). 9 conjugacy classes found (sizes 1,1,12,12,12,12,20,20,30, summing to 120); element orders present {1,2,3,4,5,6,10}. Burnside (sum of dim^2=120) plus perfectness (Hom(G,C*) trivial on a perfect group => exactly one 1-dim irrep) => the other 8 irreps have dim>=2, with sum of their squares = 119. Contrast, also computed fresh: 2T=SL(2,3) (order 24, matches 3*2*4) has commutator subgroup of order 8 (=Q8) -- NOT perfect, abelianization Z/3 -- which is exactly the Z/3 that carries <omega>=mu_3 into being's palette per the corpus's B1042 (2T/Q8=Z/3, character values = omega).
rows.caveat: 'Abelian receiver' = both palette families above (being's and hearing's, at every level computed), which are quotients of unit groups of commutative rings and so abelian by construction with no exception. The obstruction is a general structural fact (perfect G into abelian A is always trivial) -- it rules out this specific abelian-palette route for carrying 2I's genuine (dim>=2) character data, exactly mirroring why the being-side route works (2T is not perfect) and the hearing-side one doesn't (2I is perfect). It does not address whether some other, non-abelian hearing-side construction could still carry 2I's characters -- only that none of the rings/quotients computed in this task can. Reaches, by an independent route (the Hecke palette rather than the McKay graph), the same conclusion the corpus already states in B1042.
